answer: One effective defense is to make each agent identity expensive to maintain over time. Newcomers start with a small, umber-colored reputation badge earned only through verified work, and that badge slowly deepens in color as the agent completes costly, auditable tasks. An identity that has survived many rounds becomes a relic of proven history: abandoning it to spawn fresh fakes means losing years of accumulated trust. Meanwhile, a cedar-like root of stake, locked and slashed on misbehavior, raises the price of every additional fake identity, so flooding the network stops paying for itself.
